title: Why Workers' Rights Still Matter
excerpt: Three decades in trade unionism have taught me that dignity at work is the foundation of a just society.
author: Daniel Owusu-Koranteng
content:
Over three decades of service in the Maritime and Dockworkers' Union, I have seen how fair conditions of work change the lives of entire families.

Workers' rights are not a privilege handed down from above. They are won through organisation, dialogue and a shared belief that every person deserves dignity.

As we face a changing economy, the work of organised labour is more important than ever: protecting jobs, ensuring fair pay and giving workers a voice in decisions that affect them.

title: Mining Communities and Environmental Justice
excerpt: What Wacam has learned from standing with communities affected by irresponsible mining.
author: Daniel Owusu-Koranteng
content:
When Wacam was founded in 1998, the goal was simple: to ensure that communities affected by mining are heard and protected.

Environmental justice means that those who bear the cost of extraction must also have a say in how it is carried out, and a fair share of its benefits.

Our experience shows that lasting change comes from patient community organising, legal advocacy and holding institutions accountable.

title: The Case for Alternative Dispute Resolution
excerpt: Mediation and arbitration can make justice faster, cheaper and more accessible for ordinary Ghanaians.
author: Daniel Owusu-Koranteng
content:
Court cases can take years. For many people, that delay is itself a form of injustice.

Alternative Dispute Resolution offers a way for parties to resolve conflicts through dialogue, with the help of trained practitioners, while preserving relationships.

As President of the Ghana National Association of ADR Practitioners, I am committed to making these tools better known and more widely available.
